ext.description: MCP server bridging Remote-SSH (Linux) AI agents to the Windows host: run Windows commands/CLIs/scripts from Copilot, Claude Code, etc. and get stdout/stderr/exit code back. stdio + HTTP modes, explicit first-run consent, no silent config changes.
cmd.startHttp.title: WinExec MCP: Start HTTP service
cmd.stopHttp.title: WinExec MCP: Stop HTTP service
cmd.register.title: WinExec MCP: Register user mcp.json
cmd.registerProject.title: WinExec MCP: Register in this project (.vscode/mcp.json)
cmd.unregisterProject.title: WinExec MCP: Remove from this project
cmd.setupExternal.title: WinExec MCP: Configure server-side agent (SSH forwarding + project registration)
cmd.setup.title: WinExec MCP: Enable / Re-run setup (consent)
cmd.fixFirewall.title: WinExec MCP: Fix firewall permissions (administrator)
config.stdio.enabled.description: Register the bundled exe in stdio mode into the user-level mcp.json (local mode, launched by the Windows client over the Remote-SSH channel). Off by default; the first enable asks for your consent before writing mcp.json
config.http.enabled.description: HTTP instance process switch (only auto-started in remote windows) + auto connect (workbench.mcp.startServer '*'). Off by default; the first enable asks for your consent
config.http.token.description: HTTP Bearer token (leave empty to auto-generate a random token on first activation and persist it)
config.http.host.description: Manually specify a LAN IP (overrides auto-detection for multi-NIC / hotspot setups; leave empty to auto-detect and skip hotspot subnets)
